free_tier.stated: The pricing page states USD 0.04 per vCPU-hour plus USD 0.01 per GiB-hour of memory and USD 0.09 per GB of network traffic in and out, metered per MB. New organizations get USD 5 in usage credits and USD 50 more when they add a card. From December 1, 2026 disks and commits cost USD 0.10 per GiB-month.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine, not an object
per_object_cap.notes: The primary constraint is the virtual machine hardware specification.

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a machine or an account, not stored bytes
retention.notes: a machine record: what is lost is the running process, not a stored object

egress.terms: All network traffic in and out of VMs, in both directions, is metered per MB and billed at USD 0.09 per GB; there is no free allowance.

interface_detail: The docs.vers.sh CLI reference documents the standalone vers CLI binary (HTTPS control plane) and an SSH gateway at try.vers.sh; no REST API reference or SDK was read on that page.
tooling: The vers CLI, a standalone Rust binary installed locally, and the ssh try.vers.sh gateway; the CLI reference page names no SDK or API library.
chaining: Paused VMs are free, so the shape that pays off is a fleet of branched computers parked between agent steps: 100 paused branches cost nothing, and only the one being worked on bills at USD 0.04 per vCPU-hour.
limits_note: No session cap, no idle reap and no monthly minimum are published; the first thing that actually stops a fleet is the monthly card charge for whatever ran, since paused VMs accrue nothing.
binding_note: No monthly minimums, tier floors or annual commits are published. Vers is prepaid: usage is deducted hourly and new computers cannot start at a zero balance.

identity_cost.detail: New organizations receive USD 5 in usage credits without a card and USD 50 more when they add a card. The page does not state which identifier opens the account; prepaid credit is bought with a card and running computers are paused when the balance falls USD 5 below zero.

evidence.proved: USD 0.04 per vCPU-hour, 1 second granularity, no per-branch fee, paused and stopped VMs do not accrue, 4 vCPUs 24x7 for a month is USD 116.80, and new accounts get credits before a card is required
CLI defaults are 2 vCPUs and 4096 MiB memory, so the default computer costs USD 0.08 per hour at the published rate
